items.title: Don Alias interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 6, 2002
items.q: And the writers in the band were great, Larry Willis, Tony Klatka, they were great writers, they would write material for the band... I came in at the very tail end of the success you know. I was on salary. I didn’t share in any of the revenues, shall we say, in the band.

ctx.x: Oh yeah he was back in then, back in the days. And of course Blood, Sweat & Tears. That was a wonderful experience because I started playing percussion and then moved over to the drum set. Bobby Columby, who had been doing it from the beginning, decided that he wanted to stay home I guess and collect the money. And I moved over to the drum chair, and for me that was a great challenge. Again, here comes the challenge. And the writers in the band were great, Larry Willis, Tony Klatka, they were great writers, they…

Blood, Sweat and Tears sound. So they also, if you consider them a Pop group, because they were very successful. I came in at the very tail end of the success you know. I was on salary. I didn’t share in any of the revenues, shall we say, in the band.
